gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-osmanya: Wide, easy s turns and oversized lowercase make the text feel friendly. Noto Sans Osmanya, a sans-serif, sits beneath the loud poured-ink letters of Luckiest Guy and lets the shouting stay up top.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-warang-cit: Cheerful and loud, Luckiest Guy sets poured-looking letters over Noto Sans Warang Citi, whose words read as solid blocks. Wide channels into each counter keep the sans body easy to enter.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-elbasan: Sharp angles and a distinctly futuristic hum from the first letter. Megrim is at its best as a sleek, angular signal, while Noto Sans Elbasan handles the quieter work of carrying sentences.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-mende-kikakui: Noto Sans Mende Kikakui is a sans with daylight in every curve. Against the angular, futuristic lines of Megrim, that open, tall lowercase is the pair's quiet standout, easy to spot.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-old-persian: Megrim finishes every stroke with a measured, constant thickness. Its ruler-and-compass angles do the announcing, while Noto Sans Old Persian handles the reading with a sans body of lofty, breathing open counters.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Futuristic and angular, Megrim sets the tone. Noto Sans Oriya, a sans with generous curve gaps and small letters nearly as tall as the capitals, takes over for the reading.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-warang-citi: Noto Sans Warang Citi sets words as solid blocks. Megrim does the opposite job, spending its angular, futuristic lines on display, while the body font keeps channels wide into every counter.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-aldrich: Storybook charm, all open-jawed curves. Mystery Quest brings that nostalgic, bookish lean up top, and Aldrich follows cleanly with modern, single-width strokes and an x-height close to the capitals.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Noto Sans Grantha is a sans with tall little letters and bowls that never close up, so reading never snags. Mystery Quest earns its keep when big and brief.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-noto-sans-jp: Noto Sans JP reads tall and open, its sans-serif curves sweeping wide instead of curling shut, on a very tall x-height. Made small, Mystery Quest would lose its compact, bookish charm.
